basics.name: Akshay
basics.headline: Embedded Engineer — Embedded AI / Edge AI
basics.work_preference: Bengaluru or fully remote preferred; will relocate internationally for a clearly strong embedded-AI / edge-AI opportunity

_match_comment: Stage 1 of the funnel. Cheap, deterministic, runs on every ingested job.

match._include_titles_comment: A title hit is worth as much as the whole keyword basket. Keep this to the embedded/firmware family so software-only roles never clear on title alone.
match._exclude_titles_comment: Hard zero - deterministically rejected, never shown. Pure software / non-embedded roles. 'Embedded Software Engineer' still passes because 'embedded' matches include_titles first only for scoring; these are substring checks on the title, so keep them specific enough not to catch an embedded role.
match._exclude_seniority_comment: These now RANK DOWN rather than reject (see seniority_penalty). That is why 'senior' and 'lead' are safe to list here - before the penalty existed, listing them would have hard-zeroed half the embedded market. Senior JDs are keyword-dense and otherwise sweep the whole 40-row LLM budget away from the mid-level roles you are actually likely to get.
match._seniority_comment: Soft rank penalty for in-domain titles matching exclude_seniority[], NOT a kill - score.js grades the stretch with the full JD. Senior/staff JDs are keyword-dense and would otherwise sweep the whole 40-row LLM budget away from junior and mid roles. Raise toward 1.0 to see more senior stretches, lower to focus on your own level.
match._off_location_comment: Score multiplier for roles outside locations[] above. Not a kill - abroad roles still reach the LLM and the review queue, just ranked lower. Raise toward 1.0 to see more international roles, lower to focus on Bengaluru/remote.

_bullets_comment: The tailoring model may ONLY select and rephrase bullets from this inventory. Every id it returns is validated against this file before rendering. Nothing gets invented.

bullets.text: Built firmware for BLE + ANT+ wearable devices on ESP32-S3, covering sensor acquisition, power management, and OTA update paths.
Designed the Smart Jersey athlete-monitoring product end to end: hardware bring-up, firmware, ingestion API, and the dashboard coaches actually used courtside.
Integrated GPS and IMU streams into a live telemetry pipeline, handling clock skew and lossy BLE links across dozens of concurrent devices.
Ran a summer-camp deployment monitoring live athletes, then debugged the field failures that only appear with real users on real hardware.
Stood up the backend on EC2 with Docker, PM2, PostgreSQL and Cloudflare, including deploys, monitoring, and incident response.
Built React admin dashboards and mobile apps for device provisioning, live session views, and historical athlete analytics.

projects.name: Football video analysis
projects.text: Built a computer-vision pipeline using YOLO and OpenCV for player tracking and ball detection on match footage, including homography to pitch coordinates and per-player movement stats.

projects.name: STM32U585 Embedded AI Activity Recognition
projects.text: Built an on-device activity recognition system on STM32U585: IMU data acquisition at 50 Hz over a standing/walking/squatting dataset, TensorFlow Lite model training with INT8 quantization, and deployment via STM32CubeAI / X-CUBE-AI for real-time on-device inference.

projects.name: STEVAL-MKBOXPROA Sensor & Motion Processing
projects.text: Built sensor and motion processing on STM32U585 with the LSM6DSV16X IMU plus magnetometer and barometer: accelerometer/gyro/magnetometer fusion via a Mahony AHRS filter for roll/pitch/yaw estimation, including sensor calibration and debugging.

projects.name: Smart Bat / Cricket Bat Motion Tracking
projects.text: Built motion and orientation tracking for a smart cricket bat on ESP32-S3 with the QMI8658A IMU and sensor fusion, including real-time 3D bat visualization in Three.js and exploration of ball/bat detection using a high-FPS global-shutter camera.

projects.name: ESP32 Vehicle Black Box
projects.text: Built a self-contained vehicle black box on ESP32 integrating an MPU6050 IMU, GPS, GSM, and microSD: logs motion and trip events to the SD card with GPS location and timestamps, and transmits data over the cellular link. Covers the full embedded stack - multi-peripheral sensor acquisition, local storage, and remote uplink on a single MCU.

projects.name: Smart Jersey — Heart Rate Monitoring
projects.text: Built a wearable heart-rate monitoring system with BLE/ANT+ communication for sports monitoring, field-tested during a Kerala Super League summer camp.

projects.name: Polar H10 / CardioSim Heart-Rate Receiver
projects.text: Built a BLE heart-rate receiver interoperating with a Polar H10 and CardioSim III over ANT+/BLE dongles, and investigated replacing the external dongle with an STM32 MCU.

_stories_comment: Interview prep inventory (STAR format). Same guardrail as the resume bullets: src/interview/prep.js may only reference stories by their exact 'id' and select/reframe which ones answer a given question - it cannot invent a situation, action, or result that isn't written here. Fill in every REPLACE_ME with the real outcome before trusting a prep output in an actual interview.

stories.prompt: Tell me about a time you debugged a hard problem you only saw in the field, not in testing.
stories.situation: FanplayIoT's Smart Jersey wearables were deployed to monitor live athletes during a Kerala Super League summer camp.
stories.task: Keep BLE heart-rate, GPS, and IMU telemetry reliable across dozens of concurrent devices under real field conditions.
stories.action: Integrated GPS and IMU into the live telemetry pipeline, handled clock skew between devices, and worked through lossy BLE links dropping packets across many concurrent devices - debugging failures that never showed up on a bench with one device.
stories.result: REPLACE_ME - what changed after the fix (uptime/drop-rate before vs after, whether the camp ran without further incident, any number you can point to).

stories.prompt: Tell me about a project you owned end to end.
stories.situation: FanplayIoT needed an athlete-monitoring product (Smart Jersey) built from nothing.
stories.task: Take it from hardware bring-up through to something coaches would actually use courtside.
stories.action: Built the firmware for BLE + ANT+ wearables on ESP32-S3, the backend ingestion API, and the React dashboard coaches used, plus stood up the EC2/Docker/PM2/Postgres/Cloudflare infrastructure behind it.
stories.result: REPLACE_ME - adoption or usage detail (how many coaches/athletes, how it changed what they could see mid-session).

stories.prompt: Tell me about a technically challenging project outside your day job.
stories.situation: Wanted on-device activity recognition (standing/walking/squatting) running entirely on an STM32U585, no cloud round-trip.
stories.task: Get a trained ML model small and fast enough to run inference directly on the MCU in real time.
stories.action: Collected an IMU dataset at 50 Hz across the three activities, trained a TensorFlow Lite model, applied INT8 quantization to fit the target footprint, and deployed it via STM32CubeAI / X-CUBE-AI.
stories.result: REPLACE_ME - accuracy achieved, inference latency/memory footprint on-device, or anything quantified.

stories.prompt: Tell me about a production incident you handled.
stories.situation: FanplayIoT's backend (EC2, Docker, PM2, PostgreSQL, Cloudflare) served live telemetry during athlete monitoring sessions.
stories.task: Keep it up and respond fast when something broke, since the data was time-sensitive (live sessions, not batch).
stories.action: Owned deploys, monitoring, and incident response on that stack end to end.
stories.result: REPLACE_ME - a specific incident: what broke, how you found it, how long it took to fix, what you changed so it wouldn't happen again.
